names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 31 Οκτωβρίου, «Άγιος Νικόλαος από τη Χίο ο Νεομάρτυρας», with the rank words left off.

Read out of the Охридски пролог’s heading for 31. октобар ст. ст., „Св. муч. Никола Хиоски.“ — «Св. муч.» is the martyr grade this corpus keeps in `types` and comes off, leaving the bare name with the by-name the heading prints. «Хиоски» is kept under section 6: it is the island he was born and died on, which is a by-name and not a see, and it is load-bearing — the bare «Никола» is already held by `nicholas-of-magnesia` and `nicholas-the-grocer-of-karpenisi`, both of them new-martyrs of the same centuries, and the corpus keeps a great many Nicholases besides. This is the folder’s FIRST name form outside Greek.

death.note: saint.gr: «Ο Άγιος Νεομάρτυς Νικόλαος μαρτύρησε στις 31 Οκτωβρίου 1754 μ.Χ. και ώρα έκτη, στη θέση Βουνάκι της Χίου», and the heading «(; - 1754)». No year of birth is given; the page says only that he went to Magnesia at twenty.

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 31ης Οκτωβρίου — «Άγιος Νικόλαος από τη Χίο ο Νεομάρτυρας»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 31 Οκτωβρίου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing. **He is not the corpus's Nicholas of Magnesia**, although both pages have a young Chian working in Magnesia: that folder's man is born 1754 and dies 1776, of Yaya Köy, son of Hadji-Kanelos, and is kept on 24 April; this one dies at Chios on 31 October 1754, born at Karyes of Chios of Peter and Stamatou. The corpus keeps fifty-odd other Nicholases and none of them is of Chios. No location is recorded even though the page names Karyes, Vounaki and the Souda of the castle, because it is a martyrdom's places and not a seat. The apolytikion and the kontakion both name him and are taken; the Μεγαλυνάριον is neither and is not drafted. No asterisk and not the sentence «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη η ύπαρξη του Αγίου».

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 13.11.2025 (31. октобар ст. ст.) — „Св. муч. Никола Хиоски.“

attestations.note: The day’s third entry, one person, quoted whole with its closing full stop (section 4), and THIS FOLDER’S SECOND VENERATED ROW AND SECOND NAME FORM OF ANY LANGUAGE — it held one Greek form and one Greek row before today. `types` UNTOUCHED: the folder holds `new-martyr`, and the heading says «Св. муч.» while the body supplies the rest — tortured and beheaded by the Turks in 1754, which is what makes the grade a new-martyr rather than a martyr. The body’s «Побожан младић и велики ревнитељ вере Христове» is a character and not a rank, so nothing was added for it. `dates` UNTOUCHED AND EXACTLY CONFIRMED: the folder holds `death` 1754 off saint.gr’s «μαρτύρησε στις 31 Οκτωβρίου», and this entry says «посечен 1754. год.» — the same year, flat in both books. WHAT THE BOOK ADDS: THE VILLAGE. «Рођен у селу Кириаху на острву Хиосу» — born in the village of Kiriah on the island of Chios, and tortured and beheaded there, and there he gave up his righteous soul to God. The island was already the folder’s display name; the VILLAGE is new, and so is the fact that he was born and died in the same place. NO `locations` was written from it: a village this corpus has no gazetteer entry for is not a coordinate, and the folder has none. NO `related` — the entry names nobody at all. No `office`. THE FORM IS FREE BECAUSE IT KEEPS THE BY-NAME: `foldchk.py` returns `NO FOLDER HOLDS THIS FORM` for «Никола Хиоски» and names `nicholas-of-magnesia` and `nicholas-the-grocer-of-karpenisi` for the bare «Никола» — two other new-martyrs of the Turkish centuries, which is exactly the company a bare forename would have been lost in. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion.

hymns.text: Τῆς Χίου ἀγλάϊσμα, καὶ Ἀθλητῶν μιμητῆς, ἐδείχθης Νικόλαε, ὁμολογήσας Χριστόν, τυράννων ἐνώπιον· ὅθεν τῶν σῶν αἱμάτων, οἱ κρουνοὶ Ἀθλοφόρε, δρόσος ὤφθησαν θεία, τῇ Χριστοῦ Ἐκκλησίᾳ· ἐντεῦθεν πανευχαρίστως, μέλπει τοὺς ἄθλους σου.

source.text: saint.gr, Ἀπολυτίκιον, Ἦχος δ’, Ταχὺ προκατάλαβε — the first hymn on the page of «Άγιος Νικόλαος από τη Χίο ο Νεομάρτυρας». It names him and the island and no other saint.

english.text: You were shown to be the ornament of Chios and an imitator of the martyrs, Nicholas, confessing Christ before tyrants; and so the streams of your blood, prize-winner, appeared as a divine dew to the Church of Christ, which thankfully sings of your contests.

hymns.text: Φερωνύμως γέγονας, νίκη λαοῦ Ὀρθοδόξου, ἱερὲ Νικόλαε, ὑπὲρ Χριστοῦ ἐναθλήσας· ὅθεν σοι, ἐν κατανύξει ψυχῆς βοῶμεν· Δώρησαι, ἡμῖν τὴν νίκην ταῖς σαῖς πρεσβείας, κατ’ ἐχθρῶν τῶν ὁρωμένων, καὶ ἀοράτων, τοῖς σὲ τιμῶσι πιστῶς.

source.text: saint.gr, Κοντάκιον, Ἦχος γ’, Ἡ Παρθένος σήμερον — on the page of «Άγιος Νικόλαος από τη Χίο ο Νεομάρτυρας». It names him and no other saint, and plays on his name as the site's own gloss of it does.

english.text: True to your name you became the victory of the Orthodox people, holy Nicholas, by contending for Christ; and so we cry to you with compunction of soul: by your intercessions grant us, who honour you in faith, the victory over our enemies seen and unseen.
